items.stem: An array Codes holds 20 integers. (a) Write pseudocode for a bubble sort that sorts Codes into ascending order and stops early if no swaps are made in a pass. (b) Explain why the number of comparisons in each pass can be reduced by one each time.
items.answer:
Boundary ← 19
REPEAT
    NoSwaps ← TRUE
    FOR j ← 1 TO Boundary
        IF Codes[j] > Codes[j + 1] THEN
            Temp ← Codes[j]
            Codes[j] ← Codes[j + 1]
            Codes[j + 1] ← Temp
            NoSwaps ← FALSE
        ENDIF
    NEXT j
    Boundary ← Boundary - 1
UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE OR Boundary = 0
(b) After each pass the largest remaining value is in its final place at the end, so it need not be compared again.
items.markingKey: (a) outer loop until no swaps [1]; flag reset/set [1]; inner loop with correct bound [1]; comparison of adjacent elements [1]; swap using temp [1]; boundary reduced [1] (b) [1]

items.stem:
This pseudocode is one pass of a bubble sort on the array Data[1:10].
FOR j ← 1 TO 9
    IF Data[j] > Data[j + 1] THEN
        Data[j] ← Data[j + 1]
        Data[j + 1] ← Data[j]
    ENDIF
NEXT j
Identify the error and explain how to correct it.
items.answer: The swap overwrites Data[j] before it is saved, so both elements end up with the same value. Use a temporary variable: Temp ← Data[j]; Data[j] ← Data[j + 1]; Data[j + 1] ← Temp.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: error identified; 1 mark: correction [2]

An array Values[1:11] contains [61, 40, 37, 16, 82, 58, 84, 76, 17, 81, 73]. (a) Write pseudocode for a linear search that outputs the index of a value input by the user, or "Not found". (b) State the number of comparisons needed to find 82. (c) Give the array after one pass of an ascending bubble sort.
items.answer:
INPUT Target
Index ← 0
i ← 1
WHILE i <= 11 AND Index = 0
    IF Values[i] = Target THEN
        Index ← i
    ENDIF
    i ← i + 1
ENDWHILE
IF Index = 0 THEN
    OUTPUT "Not found"
ELSE
    OUTPUT Index
ENDIF
(b) 5 (c) [40, 37, 16, 61, 58, 82, 76, 17, 81, 73, 84]
items.markingKey: (a) input [1]; loop with correct bounds/stop condition [1]; comparison [1]; output index or Not found [1] (b) 5 [1] (c) [40, 37, 16, 61, 58, 82, 76, 17, 81, 73, 84] [2]

items.stem:
The text file Log.txt contains these lines, in order: Lisbon, Lagos, Cairo, Lima, Dubai, Doha.
Count ← 0
OPENFILE "Log.txt" FOR READ
WHILE NOT EOF("Log.txt")
    READFILE "Log.txt", Line
    IF LEFT(Line, 1) = "C" THEN
        OUTPUT Line
        Count ← Count + 1
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "Log.txt"
OUTPUT Count
State the output.
items.answer: Cairo 1

items.stem: Isla is writing a text editor that needs an "undo" feature. (a) Identify the most suitable ADT and justify your choice. (b) Explain what should happen if an item is added when the structure is full. (c) Write pseudocode for a procedure to add an item to the ADT you chose, implemented as an array.
items.answer: (a) Queue for printing/waiting room (FIFO); stack for undo (LIFO). (b) Report an error (overflow) and do not store the item / wait. (c) Stack: IF TopOfStack = MaxSize THEN OUTPUT "Full" ELSE TopOfStack ← TopOfStack + 1; Stack[TopOfStack] ← Item ENDIF. Queue: IF RearPointer = MaxSize THEN OUTPUT "Full" ELSE RearPointer ← RearPointer + 1; Queue[RearPointer] ← Item ENDIF
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark ADT; 1 mark justification [2] (b) 1 mark [1] (c) 1 mark full check; 1 mark increment pointer; 1 mark store item [3]
